root_causes.root_cause: Source PDF text layer has Arabic character reordering artifacts: PyMuPDF extracts 'املادة' (alef-meem-lam order) instead of 'المادة' (alef-lam-meem). NFKC normalization cannot fix character reordering. The _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE regex in helpers.py:1949 matches '(?:ال)?مادة' which requires alef-lam prefix, but the reordered 'املادة' form has meem-lam, so zero article markers match (confirmed: 0 regex matches vs 137 lines containing مادة). This prevents split_oversized_leaf_nodes from further splitting tail-blobs at article boundaries, producing a flatter tree (234 nodes) than the English version of the same law (505 nodes). The chars/page metric (~1062) is NOT converter content-loss: the raw text layer itself has only 1140 chars/page (93% preserved through Docling). The document actually improved massively from ~6K chars (Run 18) to 106K chars (Run 19). 85/100 pages contain C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F) embedded in Arabic words, further confirming a degraded text layer.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add an alternative 'املادة' pattern (reordered alef-meem-lam form) to _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE as a secondary Arabic article marker variant. This handles the specific char-reorder artifact this PDF class produces without affecting other Arabic documents. Pattern addition: r"|(?:ا)?مل(?:ا)?دة\s*\(?\s*(?P<mada2>[\d٠-٩]+)" alongside the existing مادة branch. Alternatively, add a pre-fold normalization step that detects and corrects the ملا->الم swap before NFKC folding.
